statement: Three consecutive even numbers have a product of 21840. What is their sum?

choices.misconception: I found the middle number and gave it instead of the sum.
I found the numbers 26, 28 and 30 but added only the smallest and the largest.
I thought 28 was the largest of the three numbers and added 24, 26 and 28.
I thought 28 was the smallest number, because the cube root of 21840 is nearly 28, and added 28, 30 and 32.

hints: Each choice divided by 3 gives the middle number. Test it.
The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 3 times the middle one, so each choice names a candidate middle number. Multiply out the candidate triple and compare with 21840.
The choice 84 gives the middle number 28, and $26 \times 28 \times 30 = 21840$.

solutions.reliable: The cube root of 21840 is just under 28, so the middle number is near 28. Try 26, 28, 30: $26 \times 30 = 780$ and $780 \times 28 = 21840$. The sum is $26 + 28 + 30 = 84$. Back-solving gives the same: a sum of 84 means a middle number of 28, and that triple works, while the other choices either are not multiples of 6 or give triples with the wrong product. The transferable idea: when the answers are numbers, testing a choice can be faster than solving forwards.

whyOnTest: Testing the choices, each one naming a middle number, is quicker than solving a cubic equation.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
